name: Templo de Debod — site of the Cuartel de la Montaña
story: Here stood the Montaña barracks, where General Joaquín Fanjul rose for the coup in Madrid on 19 July 1936 and then found himself besieged. On 20 July, armed workers, Assault Guards and loyal troops attacked with artillery and aircraft and stormed it; many of the officers and soldiers inside were killed after the surrender, and Fanjul was later tried and shot. The fall of the barracks secured Madrid for the Republic. The ruined building was demolished after the war, and the Egyptian Temple of Debod was re-erected on the site in 1972.
see: A park with the Egyptian temple; there is no trace of the barracks, but the viewpoint looks towards the Casa de Campo front.
plan: Free park, a short walk from Plaza de España. Best at sunset.
